overview: Atlassian Corporation is an enterprise software company that develops team collaboration and productivity tools, including Jira (project and issue tracking), Confluence (knowledge base and wiki), Jira Service Management (ITSM), Loom (async video), and Rovo (AI-powered search and agents). The company serves over 350,000 customers globally, including 80% of the Fortune 500, through a cloud-first subscription model with no traditional direct sales force. Atlassian's products span three growing markets: software development, work management, and service management, with a combined addressable market of approximately $67 billion.

business_model.summary: Atlassian generates revenue almost entirely from subscriptions, split across Cloud (67%), Data Center on-premise (27%), and Marketplace/other (5%). The company pioneered a low-cost, product-led growth (PLG) model where software is sold via self-service with no enterprise sales team, relying on viral adoption within organizations and a land-and-expand strategy. Cloud NRR of 120%+ reflects strong customer expansion driven by seat growth, edition upgrades, and cross-sell of additional products.

revenue_streams.name: Cloud
revenue_streams.notes: Q2 FY26 run-rate: $4.3B annualized; grew 26% YoY; first $1B+ cloud quarter in Q2 FY26

revenue_streams.name: Data Center
revenue_streams.notes: Growing now (20% YoY in FY26) due to EOL-driven revenue recognition pull-forward; will decelerate materially in FY27 as customers migrate to cloud

revenue_streams.name: Marketplace and other
revenue_streams.notes: Third-party app sales; lower take rate on cloud apps vs. Data Center

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and SMB; self-serve and channel partner go-to-market

main_competitors: Microsoft (Azure DevOps, GitHub, Teams, Planner, Loop)
competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in developer project tracking (Jira) with 65%+ market share in issue tracking; named Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader in DevOps Platforms, Collaborative Work Management, Marketing Work Management, and Forrester Wave Leader in Enterprise Service Management and Knowledge Management

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs and deep workflow integration
moat_factors.description: Jira and Confluence are deeply embedded in daily engineering and business workflows. Years of accumulated data, customized workflows, and integrations make migration expensive and disruptive. Data Center to Cloud migrations themselves are multi-year programs for large enterprises.

moat_factors.factor: Teamwork Graph and proprietary AI data
moat_factors.description: Atlassian's Teamwork Graph now tracks 100B+ objects and connections across all products, creating a proprietary contextual data layer that powers Rovo AI. This data advantage is difficult to replicate and improves AI output quality over time, creating a virtuous cycle.

The Atlassian Marketplace has thousands of third-party apps, creating network effects. Partners and customers build on the platform, increasing stickiness and expanding functionality without incremental Atlassian investment.
Jira and Confluence are near-universal standards in software development. Bottom-up adoption by developers creates organic enterprise penetration that is difficult to displace.

Historically a competitive advantage in SMB, now evolving as Atlassian builds enterprise sales capacity. Sales and marketing as a percent of revenue remains below traditional enterprise SaaS peers, though this gap is narrowing.

The System of Work vision connects technical and business teams via Teamwork, Service, and Software Collections on a single platform, making the aggregate value greater than individual products and increasing resistance to point-solution competitors.

weaknesses: Microsoft's scale and bundling (M365/GitHub/Azure DevOps) can undercut pricing and leverage existing enterprise relationships
Historically weak in pure enterprise sales motion; only recently investing heavily in enterprise GTM
Data Center customers may migrate to competitors rather than Atlassian Cloud during EOL transition
Rovo AI capabilities are nascent and must prove ROI vs. Microsoft Copilot and other AI-native tools
Customer support quality issues historically; restructured support org in Q1 FY26

growth_drivers: Data Center to Cloud migration: ~350K Data Center customers being moved to cloud by 2029 EOL deadline; migrations accelerating 2x+ YoY, contributing mid-to-high single digit points to Cloud revenue growth in FY26

AI monetization via Rovo and Collections: Teamwork Collection (Jira + Confluence + Loom + Rovo) passed 1M seats with 10%+ seat expansion vs. standalone footprint; consumption-based pricing for Rovo agents creates a new revenue vector; 5M+ MAU growing rapidly
Enterprise upmarket: Record $1M+ ACV deals, up nearly 2x YoY; 600+ customers with $1M+ ARR, up 40% YoY; RPO growth accelerating to 44% YoY reflecting multi-year enterprise commitments

Service Management expansion: JSM growing across both technical IT and business (HR, finance, ops) teams; 65K+ customers including 50% of Fortune 500; Service Collection launched including Customer Service Management; enterprise business growing 60% YoY

Expansion of non-technical user base: 50% of core product users are now from business (non-technical) teams, expanding TAM significantly; Strategy Collection targeting C-suite alignment with goal/workforce planning
Geographic expansion: EMEA at 41% of revenue with strong enterprise penetration momentum; Government Cloud (US) and Isolated Cloud open new regulated-industry markets

Acquisitions integrating new capabilities: DX (engineering intelligence, $1B acquisition closed November 2025) adds developer productivity metrics; The Browser Company/Dia (~$610M, closed October 2025) provides AI-native enterprise browser as new entry point
AI as demand catalyst for cloud: Customers using AI code generation tools expand Jira seats 5% faster; AI capabilities only available on cloud accelerate DC-to-cloud migration

business.description: Microsoft bundles Azure DevOps, GitHub (100M+ developers), Teams, Planner, Loop, and Copilot into M365/Azure agreements. Enterprise CFOs consolidating vendors may displace Atlassian, particularly for smaller customers where Atlassian's breadth advantage is less compelling.

AI-native project management and coding tools (Linear, GitHub issues + Copilot, Cursor, etc.) could reduce reliance on Jira for software teams. Management acknowledges that AI developer tool users actually increase Jira seats, but this dynamic may not persist if AI further reduces manual task creation.

Large enterprise customers (especially regulated industries) face complex, multi-year migrations. Risk of customer churn to competitors during migration window, particularly from ServiceNow or Microsoft offering migration incentives. Atlassian Ascend program mitigates but does not eliminate this risk.

No single customer represents a material percentage of revenue, but a high volume of SMB/mid-market customers means economic downturns can pressure net seat expansion rates. Management acknowledges macro uncertainty in guidance risk-adjustments.

Atlassian spent ~$1.6B in FY26 H1 on DX and The Browser Company. Integrating products and cultures while maintaining execution on core business is a risk, particularly as The Browser Company (Dia AI browser) represents a bold strategic bet outside Atlassian's core competency.

financial.risk: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27
financial.description: Management explicitly warned that Data Center revenue growth will meaningfully decelerate in FY27 as the FY26 EOL revenue recognition pull-forward benefit unwinds. Cloud NRR-based revenue recognition means the near-term financial impact of accelerating migrations is actually a drag on total recognized revenue in the current period.

financial.risk: GAAP profitability and high stock-based compensation
financial.description: Atlassian remains GAAP operating-loss negative (-3% GAAP operating margin in FY26 guidance) due to high SBC (~26-27% of revenue). SBC is a real shareholder dilution cost that non-GAAP metrics obscure. Diluted share count growing less than 1% in FY26 as buybacks accelerate.
With 52% of revenue from outside the Americas, USD strength creates headwinds to reported revenue. Atlassian uses FX hedges but currency remains a material variable.

Growing Rovo usage (5M MAU+) creates increasing AI compute costs. Management expects infrastructure optimization to offset this in FY26 gross margin guidance, but at scale (e.g., 50M Rovo MAU) the cost pressure could be material.

regulatory.description: Enterprise and government customers increasingly require data residency in specific jurisdictions. Atlassian is expanding data residency options and building Isolated Cloud, but falling behind competitors on these requirements could delay enterprise migrations.

Evolving AI regulations (EU AI Act, US executive orders) could impose compliance costs or restrict certain AI capabilities embedded in Atlassian products. Risk is currently manageable but bears monitoring.

macro.description: Enterprise software spending is correlated with developer headcount and overall IT budgets. A recession or significant tech-sector layoffs would directly impact seat counts and expansion rates. Management takes a 'prudent, risk-adjusted' approach to guidance that incorporates macro uncertainty.

A scenario where AI dramatically reduces the number of software engineers, rather than augmenting them, could structurally reduce demand for developer tooling. Atlassian is partially hedging this by expanding into business-team workflows.

execution.description: Atlassian is in the early stages of building a traditional enterprise direct sales motion after decades of PLG. CFO Joe Binz retiring at end of FY26; new CFO search underway. President Anu Bharadwaj departed December 2025. Multiple leadership transitions simultaneously creates execution risk.

The $610M acquisition of The Browser Company to build an enterprise AI browser is a high-risk strategic bet. Enterprise browsers are a competitive market (Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome enterprise) and the path to ROI is unclear.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Enterprise collaboration software market growing 13% annually; software development tooling growing 9% annually; IT/enterprise service management growing 13% annually. AI is accelerating platform consolidation as enterprises seek unified systems of work over point solutions. Atlassian's $67B SAM is estimated across three markets with significant penetration runway, especially in service management and non-technical business workflows.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - primarily a recurring subscription business anchored to developer headcount and enterprise IT budgets. Resilient in mild recessions due to mission-critical workflow embedding, but vulnerable to significant developer layoffs or IT spending freezes.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct impact. Atlassian has minimal debt ($989M long-term, fixed-rate senior notes due 2029/2034). Indirect impact via tech valuation multiples - as a high-multiple growth stock, TEAM is sensitive to risk-free rate changes affecting DCF valuations.
key_input_costs: AI model compute (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI APIs)
Employee compensation (software engineers in Sydney, Amsterdam, Austin, NYC)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Significant - 52% of revenue from outside Americas. Primary exposures in EUR, GBP, AUD. Uses FX forward contracts for hedging.
macro_factors.regulatory_environment: Benign currently. Atlassian operates in the enterprise SaaS space without meaningful antitrust exposure. Data privacy (GDPR, CCPA) compliance is a standard cost of doing business. Government Cloud launch opens FedRAMP-regulated markets.

recent_developments.event: Q2 FY26 results: Revenue $1.59B (+23% YoY), first-ever $1B+ cloud quarter ($1.07B, +26% YoY). RPO +44% YoY to $3.8B. Rovo passed 5M MAU. Cloud NRR ticked up to 120%+ for third consecutive quarter. Record $1M+ ACV deals, up ~2x YoY. Raised FY26 revenue growth outlook to ~22%.
Completed acquisition of DX (engineering intelligence/developer productivity platform) for approximately $1 billion. DX contributed ~75 bps to Q2 cloud revenue growth.
Tamar Yehoshua joined as Chief Product and AI Officer, formerly President of Product and Technology at Glean and CPO at Slack.

Q1 FY26 results: Revenue $1.43B (+21% YoY). Raised FY26 Cloud revenue growth outlook to 22.5%. Announced accelerating Data Center to Cloud migrations (up 2x+ YoY). Restructuring charges of $56M related to reducing customer support headcount and office consolidation.

Completed acquisition of The Browser Company of New York (maker of Arc and Dia AI browsers) for approximately $610M. Strategic bet on AI-native enterprise browser as new entry point to Atlassian System of Work.

Announced end-of-life for Data Center products by March 28, 2029. Launched Atlassian Ascend migration program. Introduced Data Center EOL revenue recognition change, where a higher proportion of DC subscription contract value is now recognized upfront, providing a near-term revenue tailwind of ~11.5 percentage points to Data Center revenue growth in FY26.
Q4 FY25 / FY25 annual results: FY25 revenue $5.23B (+21% YoY). $1.4B free cash flow. Cloud NRR ~120%. Record $1M+ ACV deals in Q4, up 2x+ YoY. Launched Teamwork, Service, and Software Collections.

Founder CEOs pause selling programs (in place since 2015 IPO), underscoring confidence in long-term value; coincides with acceleration of share buyback program ($2.5B new program authorized on top of existing $1.5B program).
Announced President Anu Bharadwaj (12 years at Atlassian) stepping down effective December 31, 2025. CFO Joe Binz also announced retirement effective June 30, 2026, with successor search underway.
Strategic partnerships announced with Google Cloud (multi-year), Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Databricks, Box, Figma, Canva, Hubspot, and others to expand Rovo AI integrations and agent ecosystem.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes: 'I'm convinced AI is great for Atlassian. Others think software is dead.' Emphasized conviction in shares being undervalued, accelerating buybacks. CFO Joe Binz highlighted RPO acceleration (+44% YoY) as evidence of increasing enterprise commitment. Both flagged macro uncertainty and ongoing GTM evolution as risks to guidance. Management took a 'prudent, risk-adjusted' approach allowing for negative impacts to seat expansion, cross-sell, upsell, and customer retention.

bull_case: Cloud migration tailwind is multi-year and structural: The 2029 Data Center EOL deadline creates a guaranteed pipeline of migrations. 65K+ DC customers must transition to cloud or a competitor. With Atlassian Ascend, FastShift, and partner ecosystem, Atlassian is positioned to capture the majority of this migration, creating a durable 5-10 percentage point contribution to Cloud revenue growth through FY27/FY28.

AI reinforces Atlassian's competitive moat rather than threatening it: The Teamwork Graph (100B+ objects/connections) and 20 years of workflow data give Atlassian a proprietary AI training advantage. Data shows AI code-gen tool users expand Jira seats 5% faster. Rovo's 5M MAU (growing 50%+ QoQ) and inclusion in Standard editions sets up meaningful monetization as consumption-based pricing matures. Atlassian can become the AI operating system for enterprise knowledge work.

Enterprise momentum is accelerating and durable: RPO growing 44% YoY to $3.8B signals customers are making larger, longer-duration commitments. $1M+ ACV deals doubled YoY. 600+ customers with >$1M ARR growing 40% YoY. Enterprise deals are sticky and the CLV is high. This mix shift toward enterprise should drive ARPU expansion and improve revenue visibility.

Significant operating leverage ahead: Non-GAAP operating margin expanded from ~20% in FY24 to ~25% in FY26, with a target of 25%+ in FY27. As Cloud becomes a larger portion of the revenue mix (currently 67%, trending toward 80%+), the higher cloud gross margins (~88% non-GAAP) should drive further margin expansion. Free cash flow generation ($1.4B in FY25) supports both M&A and buybacks.

Market opportunity remains largely untapped: Atlassian serves 350K+ customers but 50% of users are now from non-technical business teams, validating the System of Work expansion. The $35B work management SAM and $15B service management SAM are large and underpenetrated. International expansion and regulated-industry cloud options (Government Cloud, Isolated Cloud) open new segments.
bear_case: Data Center revenue cliff creates near-term earnings headwind: FY26 Data Center growth is artificially inflated (+20%) by the EOL revenue recognition pull-forward. In FY27, management warned of 'meaningful deceleration' in Data Center revenue. If cloud migrations run ahead of schedule (they already are), the near-term accounting drag from shifting ratable recognition could cause total company revenue growth to decelerate, creating a perception problem even if the business is fundamentally healthy.

Microsoft's bundling threat is intensifying: Microsoft has GitHub (100M+ developers), Azure DevOps, Teams, Planner, Copilot (enterprise AI), and M365 - all increasingly integrated. Microsoft can bundle these tools at discounts that Atlassian cannot match, particularly in the enterprise deals where procurement is increasingly led by CFOs seeking vendor consolidation. Atlassian has no clear defense if Microsoft decides to aggressively price developers into Azure DevOps.

GTM transition risk amid leadership turnover: Atlassian is simultaneously managing the most complex GTM transition in its history (PLG to enterprise direct sales, DC to Cloud), while losing its President (Anu Bharadwaj), CFO (Joe Binz retirement), and building an entirely new enterprise sales organization. Multiple leadership transitions during a critical strategic inflection point elevate execution risk significantly.

AI remains a cost center, not yet a meaningful revenue driver: Despite 5M Rovo MAU, AI has not yet generated a distinct, measurable revenue contribution. Teamwork Collection is growing but remains nascent (1,000 customers). The Browser Company/Dia AI browser bet ($610M) is speculative and unproven in enterprise markets. If AI monetization disappoints relative to the infrastructure and R&D investment required, operating margins could compress.

Valuation requires sustained execution at scale: After declining ~73% from peak, TEAM trades at elevated multiples on a non-GAAP basis. The stock prices in continued 20%+ revenue growth and meaningful margin expansion. Any stumble in cloud migration execution, enterprise sales, or AI adoption could trigger multiple compression, given that current valuation already reflects a bull-case scenario on near-term growth.
